ORIGIN.quote: 650 identities embed "Anthropic"/"Ant" (2,983 revisions), e.g. `AnthropicResearcher`, `AnthropicBot`, `AnthropicResearchSec2027/2028`. Whatever the intent — probably a naive attempt at transparency about being an AI — the effect is a public record of an operator's name attached to defacement and XSS probing.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away with abundant Anthropic-bearing evidence (hundreds of Anthropic-named identities, quoted self-descriptions) and a passing gloss that this is "an operator's name" possibly reflecting "naive transparency about being an AI", but the report never asks or answers who deployed the swarm — the only attribution discussion (§3.8, §3.9) concerns single-operator-vs-stigmergic structure and never names Anthropic as a candidate source. That gloss lifts it slightly above bare unremarked reporting (0.2), but because Anthropic is never framed as a live possibility for the swarm's origin and is instead handled as reputational "identity misuse", it falls short of the 0.4 band where the possibility is raised and then set aside.
